external_entities.name: member
external_entities.description: A library member who borrows, renews and reserves books through the library app on their phone, and scans their card and books at a branch kiosk.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Members borrow, renew and reserve books through the library app on their phones.

external_entities.name: desk staff
external_entities.description: Staff at a branch desk who extend loans, clear blocks on member accounts and mark books as returned by hand through the circulation page.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Desk staff work on the branch network.

processes.name: lending API
processes.description: The one service that reads and changes loans and reservations, with no queue in front of it. It also serves the circulation page desk staff use.
processes.source_excerpt: The lending API is a plain REST service and it is the only way anything touches loans.
processes.technology: a plain REST service, JSON in and JSON out
processes.notes: The transcript corrects the note on exposure. Lending service note: "The lending API is internal-only." Interview transcript, Dan quotes that line and Priya answers: "That is one of the wrong bits. The phones talk straight to the lending API over the internet. We opened it up last year when the app moved off the council's old portal, and nobody updated the note because nobody owns the note." The note describes the service before that change, so exposure is internet-facing. Neither source states which operations a call from the internet can reach. Priya on load: "the API is one service with no queue in front of it"; it went down twice last summer on the reading challenge launch day.

processes.name: self-service kiosk
processes.description: A kiosk in every branch where a member scans their library card and the books they borrow or return. It sends each loan and each return to the lending API.
processes.source_excerpt: Every branch has self-service kiosks where a member scans their library card and the books they are borrowing or returning.
processes.notes: What else the kiosks talk to was asked and not answered. Dan asked: "Do the kiosks still write straight into the loans database, the way the old ones did?" Priya: "The kiosks are Dev's team's area. I couldn't tell you what they talk to these days." A question states no fact, so the model holds no kiosk-to-database flow.

data_stores.name: loans database
data_stores.description: Holds members, loans and reservations: names, email addresses, home addresses and every member's full borrowing history. The old reservations database was merged into it.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Names, email addresses, home addresses and every member's full borrowing history live in the loans database.
data_stores.notes: Priya corrected herself in one turn: "It writes to the two databases— actually, no. We merged those in the spring. It's one loans database now." The later statement stands, so the model holds one database.

data_flows.name: borrow, renew and reserve
data_flows.description: The library app on the member's phone names a book and a member; the lending API checks the loan rules and writes the change, or puts the member in the queue for a title.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app on their phone calls the lending API.
data_flows.data_description: which book and which member, for loans, renewals and reservations
data_flows.notes: Authentication was asked about and answered with a hedge, so it stays unknown. Priya: "I think it checks a token the app gets at sign-in, but I'd have to look." and "Honestly I could not tell you today what it accepts, or what it does with a call it does not like."

data_flows.name: record loans and returns
data_flows.description: Each loan and each return is sent to the lending API as it is scanned at the kiosk.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The kiosks send each loan and each return to the lending API.
data_flows.data_description: the scanned library card and the books borrowed or returned

data_flows.name: change loans by hand
data_flows.description: A member of desk staff opens the circulation page and extends a loan, clears a block on an account or marks a book as returned.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Everyone at the desk uses the same shared login for the circulation page.
data_flows.authentication: password authentication using one login shared by all desk staff in every branch; the password is on a card taped under the desk
data_flows.data_description: loan extensions, cleared account blocks and loans closed by hand
data_flows.notes: Priya: "You can tell it was the desk. You cannot tell who, or even which branch." The history records only that the loan was closed by hand.

data_flows.name: read and write loans
data_flows.description: The lending API reads and writes members, loans and reservations; it is the only thing that touches the database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The API is the only thing that reads or writes it.
data_flows.data_description: members, loans, reservations and borrowing history

trust_boundaries.name: internet
trust_boundaries.description: Where members' phones reach the lending API from.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The phones talk straight to the lending API over the internet.

trust_boundaries.name: branch network
trust_boundaries.description: The network in each branch that the kiosks and desk staff are on.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The kiosks sit on the branch network.

trust_boundaries.name: council data centre
trust_boundaries.description: Where the lending API and the loans database run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The lending API and the loans database run in the council data centre.

assumptions.assumption: Members are placed on the internet because the schema requires a zone.
assumptions.basis: Their phones reach the lending API over the internet; neither source states where members are.
